atoms.name: Reconstruct continuity from durable state only
atoms.statement: A fresh agent must reconstruct valid continuation from the repository and canonical harness state alone; any continuation-critical fact held elsewhere is a defect.
atoms.mechanism: Master Goal O1 and AGENTS.md rule 1; audits prove it by running full lifecycles in fresh processes with empty HOME/CODEX_HOME using only plan, ledger, head and evidence files.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 must rebuild every decision from its own observed ledger, never from omp session state.

atoms.name: Ephemeral context is never authority
atoms.statement: Conversation, memory, summaries, transcripts, handoffs, sessions and compaction output are disposable inputs and must never serve as authority.
atoms.mechanism: O2; the spec checker rejects text granting them authority, production code has no read path to them, and an E2E proves an ephemeral nonce is unrecoverable from authority after real /clear boundaries.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: treat omp transcripts and compaction summaries as untrusted model-authored input.

atoms.name: Each turn is a bounded fail-closed slice
atoms.statement: Every disposable turn performs a bounded slice of work and either durably progresses or pauses fail-closed; multi-turn work continues only through durable state.
atoms.mechanism: O1; the one-shot fresh-turn adapter classifies each turn into typed outcomes (active, no_durable_progress, blocked, typed errors) from before/after canonical snapshots.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 should close every omp turn with a harness-computed durable-delta verdict.

atoms.name: Task completion never implies Goal completion
atoms.statement: Completing an atomic task proves only that task's contract and never implies completion of the overall Goal.
atoms.mechanism: O3; the checker rejects TaskComplete-implies-GoalComplete wording, and supervisor/driver protocols treat an active child's goal_complete or a selector's task_complete as invalid.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: stops an agent from parlaying one green task into a 'done' claim.

atoms.name: Hard gates before any authority
atoms.statement: A candidate becomes authority only after hard invariants, deterministic task verification, frozen anchors, history preservation and context independence all pass.
atoms.mechanism: O4; each task's Public Verify (full suite, lint, contract checker, hook render check, smoke, ledger verify) runs as a root subprocess and must yield a success receipt before explicit completion.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: in G1 only harness-executed gates can promote a change.

atoms.name: Model reports and opinions are not authority
atoms.statement: Preferences, model reports, a bare process exit and audit opinions are never authority; findings count only after reproduction and acceptance.
atoms.mechanism: O4; completion reads only root-appended receipts and recomputed digests, the verify skill forbids converting self-report into evidence, and audits reproduce each finding by command.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: this is G1's founding rule; extend it to all LLM text.

atoms.name: Reject dominated higher-complexity candidates
atoms.statement: Reject any candidate dominated by a known capability-equivalent lower-complexity candidate, and freeze only after a delete-first test finds no equivalent reduction.
atoms.mechanism: O7 and P10; audits run delete-first/minimality challenges with line-level LOC classification and issued DELETE verdicts (PreToolUse, cache, route/delegate, resume, migration, oracle, Stop).
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: every G1 mechanism should be justified by a reproduced threat or deleted.

atoms.name: Preserve native agent capabilities
atoms.statement: The harness must not override the host agent's reasoning, tools, permissions, sandboxing, approvals, retries, subagents, models, providers or transport.
atoms.mechanism: O9 and AGENTS.md; T1 has no ordinary-tool hook, no approval reimplementation and no model routing, and smoke plus deletion tests show native tools run unchanged.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: G1 may observe and record every omp tool call but should gate only completion claims, not ordinary tools.

atoms.name: Goal spec is inert; progress derived
atoms.statement: The normative Goal spec stores no progress and adds no runtime or canonical surface; satisfaction is derived on demand from source, contracts, ledger and current receipts.
atoms.mechanism: Authority section and O11; the checker pins MUTABLE_GOAL_STATE and both SURFACE fields to none and forbids CURRENT_TASK, NEXT_TASK, TASK_QUEUE, PROGRESS and *_SCORE fields.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: no mutable progress file an agent could edit to fake advancement.

atoms.name: Lessons persist only as verified artifacts
atoms.statement: Meta-improvements persist only as verified code, tests, specs or deterministic procedures with anchors intact; lessons-memory, self-approval and weaker verifiers never count as gains.
atoms.mechanism: O12; the checker forbids 'meta-improvement persists only as lessons', 'weaker verifier allowed' and 'self-approval sufficient' phrasings.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: encode G1 lessons as tests/checks, never as prompt notes or memory.

atoms.name: Accepted steps require strict gain
atoms.statement: Each accepted step preserves invariants and verified capability and strictly reduces the unsatisfied goal set, improves verified capability, or reduces complexity at equal capability.
atoms.mechanism: O6; enforced procedurally by independent audits (capability-regression checks, LOC/surface deltas) and by forbidden checker phrases, not by runtime code.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: experiment: needs a progress predicate G1 can compute itself instead of audit judgement.

atoms.name: Finite objective terminality, no scores
atoms.statement: The Goal is a finite set of terminal properties satisfied exactly when none is unsatisfied; percentages, intelligence scalars and subjective scores are never authority.
atoms.mechanism: O5; the checker rejects percent literals and SCORE/PROGRESS fields and requires 1-10 sequentially numbered terminal properties covering T1-T10.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: an LLM-produced score must never decide done-ness.

atoms.name: Goal completion bound to current receipt
atoms.statement: Goal completion requires current deterministic Goal verification and an explicit completion bound to that successful receipt; model declarations, stale verification and unbound reports are rejected.
atoms.mechanism: O8; goal_complete is derived only from a completed final-verification task evaluated with require_current=True whose transition matches the receipt seq/hash, re-checked on a second stable observation.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: done-ness is a fresh harness re-verification, never a stored flag.

atoms.name: No-active boundary registers one smallest task
atoms.statement: At a no-active boundary with an unsatisfied property, one fresh native turn records gap/justification fields and registers exactly one smallest justified task by fixed priority (integrity > continuity > capability > native > minimality > convenience); with nothing unsatisfied it creates no task and runs only final verification.
atoms.mechanism: O10 and read policy; the optional one-shot selector validates the registered contract and attributes it to its own invocation nonce.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep one-task-at-a-time, but G1 can only validate the selection's structure, not the model's justification.

atoms.name: Forbidden selection anti-patterns
atoms.statement: Selection must never yield a giant complete-everything task, simultaneous active tasks, a hidden mutable queue, conversation-carried selection, supervisor reasoning or model routing.
atoms.mechanism: O10 REJECT list mirrored as checker forbidden patterns; AST/source tests assert the supervisor and driver contain no model invocation or planning.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 orchestration must stay mechanical and non-planning.

atoms.name: Terminal evidence deterministic and reproducible
atoms.statement: Each terminal property stays false until its evidence (commands, exits, hashes, receipts, tests, inventories) is reproducible from durable state; vague terms such as 'good enough' are rejected.
atoms.mechanism: The checker requires a deterministic evidence token in every P-section and rejects a list of vague phrases.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: every G1 acceptance criterion must name a command, hash or receipt.

atoms.name: Every P0-P2 finding maps to receipt
atoms.statement: Audit resolution requires every P0/P1/P2 finding to map to a remediation receipt or an explicit exclusion, with environment, revisions, commands, exits and hashes recorded.
atoms.mechanism: P09; each re-audit names one next remediation task and the following re-audit independently reproduces the closure before readiness flips.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 findings close only by harness-verified receipts, never by agent assertion.

atoms.name: Optional layers removable without damage
atoms.statement: Optional execution layers must be deletable without canonical migration while leaving the core and the native agent operational.
atoms.mechanism: O11 and P08; deletion tests remove each adapter, supervisor and driver and re-run the core lifecycle.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: uninstalling G1 must leave omp fully functional.

atoms.name: Restart recovery proven by hash equality
atoms.statement: Crash/restart recovery is accepted only when real kill/restart tests reproduce identical plan/ledger/head/source/tree/artifact hashes and pass ledger verification.
atoms.mechanism: P06; real processes are killed at every write boundary (sitecustomize os._exit shims) and recovery must converge to exactly one transition.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: inject real process kills at every G1 write boundary.

atoms.name: Sterile isolation for end-to-end evidence
atoms.statement: End-to-end continuity claims require isolated runs with empty user/runtime directories that exclude ephemeral authority and bind a verification receipt.
atoms.mechanism: P04; native E2E builds empty runtime dirs, admits only auth plus sanitized config, excludes continuity env IDs and seals evidence into a root receipt.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1's own E2E proofs need empty HOME/config to rule out hidden state.

atoms.name: Unproven failure types stay unclaimed
atoms.statement: Only boundary and failure types backed by a source matrix and tests are supported; unproven approval/transient types remain unclaimed and are never blindly retried or inferred.
atoms.mechanism: P07; adapters and supervisors are retry-free, pausing or stopping on every typed error, and launch failures are not retried.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: no blind retries on unclassified omp/provider errors.

atoms.name: Deferred scope declared and pinned
atoms.statement: Later-goal exclusions are listed explicitly and the checker pins the exact exclusion set so scope cannot silently grow or shrink.
atoms.mechanism: EXCLUDED_LATER line in the spec compared set-wise against a constant in the checker.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 should state what it does not verify.

atoms.name: Bounded on-demand spec reading
atoms.statement: With an active task, read only the instruction file, the task contract and canonical state; read the Goal spec only at a no-active boundary or when the contract targets a terminal property.
atoms.mechanism: Read policy; the selector exits not-applicable without reading the Goal when a task is active, and hooks never read the Goal.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: limit G1 context injection, noting G1 cannot verify what the model actually read.

atoms.name: No completion claim without current evidence
atoms.statement: Never claim a task complete without current evidence; reports must separate passed, failed and unverified facts, cite paths/receipts and avoid confidence language.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md rule plus report/verify skills; mechanically, plan --status complete and report --require-complete share one evaluator that refuses without a valid current receipt.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: in G1 the claim gate is mechanical and chat claims are ignored.

atoms.name: Opt-in enrollment, narrow harness scope
atoms.statement: The harness is used only for durable continuity and verification; work not enrolled via task begin remains valid native work with no harness continuity claim.
atoms.mechanism: Template plan holds zero tasks; task begin atomically creates the first contract; unenrolled work is untouched.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: G1 observes all turns but issues verification claims only for enrolled tasks.

atoms.name: No host-specific paths in canonical rules
atoms.statement: Optional external copies are never required for correctness, and canonical instructions/specs must not assume host paths, models, providers or hosts.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md rule (remediated from a mandatory /sdcard copy); the checker forbids /home,/root,/Users,/data,/sdcard paths and REQUIRED_MODEL/PROVIDER/HOST/HOST_PATH fields in the Goal spec.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 rules must run identically on any host.

atoms.name: Always-read instruction budget
atoms.statement: The always-loaded agent instruction file is capped at 2048 bytes to bound per-turn context and interpretation cost.
atoms.mechanism: check_agents fails the contract check when AGENTS.md exceeds 2048 bytes.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: cap G1's injected instructions per turn.

atoms.name: Stdlib-only with zero runtime dependencies
atoms.statement: Production code depends only on the language standard library plus Git, and the dependency list is pinned empty by test.
atoms.mechanism: pyproject dependencies = [] asserted by the anchor test; README declares Python 3.11+ and Git only.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the zero-dependency discipline in G1's own runtime language.

atoms.name: Exactly one active task
atoms.statement: At most one task is active; more than one is a typed current_task_ambiguous error, and pending/blocked tasks stay parked and unprojected.
atoms.mechanism: Plan parser and every surface fail closed on multiple actives; activation and begin are serialized under the ledger lock with typed losers.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: one active claim surface keeps attribution unambiguous.

atoms.name: Explicit scoped idempotent invalidation
atoms.statement: Retraction is explicit: one reason-bearing invalidation record per task, appended without running commands or rewriting evidence, idempotent and task-scoped.
atoms.mechanism: harnessctl task invalidate appends task_invalidated under the exclusive lock after an in-lock existence check; completion then fails with VERIFICATION_INVALIDATED.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 needs an append-only retraction instead of edits.

atoms.name: Weaker evidence labelled, never upgraded
atoms.statement: Evidence lacking a binding is labelled as such (legacy-output-unbound, legacy-prefix, null tri-state) and never presented as bound or as current-repository verification.
atoms.mechanism: Reports expose completion_binding and evidence_mode fields; the report skill forbids presenting historical completion as current verification.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: every G1 verdict should carry its binding strength.

atoms.name: Hooks are read-only bounded projections
atoms.statement: Host hooks only project bounded (512-byte) derived state, write nothing, fail open, and never intercept ordinary tool calls.
atoms.mechanism: Generated manifest has only SessionStart with additionalContextLimit 512; projection errors become a systemMessage; zero-write proven by full-tree snapshots.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: G1 hooks may append to G1's own observation log but must not gate tools or mutate task state.

atoms.name: Host trust observed, never inferred
atoms.statement: Hook activation is reported from the host's own trust state (installed, trusted and active are distinct); automation never touches user trust and is labelled transport-only.
atoms.mechanism: doctor --codex-hooks queries app-server hooks/list; smoke uses an isolated home and records normal_trust_activation_proven=false.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: prove G1 is actually loaded in omp from observed events, never from config presence.

atoms.name: Generated config is drift-checked
atoms.statement: Host configuration is generated from code and verified byte-equal by a check mode; hand edits are drift failures.
atoms.mechanism: render_hooks.py writes or --check compares the manifest; check_contracts also requires exactly one command hook per event sharing one executable wrapper.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: generate G1's omp extension config and diff it every run.

atoms.name: Runtime state local; contract tracked
atoms.statement: Ledger, head, pending journal, locks, evidence and private runtime are git-ignored local state, while the canonical plan must stay tracked.
atoms.mechanism: check_ignore_contract runs git check-ignore on representative runtime paths and fails if .harness/plan.md is ignored.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep G1 evidence out of agent-committed paths; cross-host moves must carry it explicitly.

atoms.name: Spec checked by structure and contradiction corpus
atoms.statement: The normative spec is validated by a deterministic checker: 12 obligations each with MUST and one REJECT counterexample, numbered terminals, one spec file, semantic signatures and a forbidden-contradiction corpus.
atoms.mechanism: master_goal_failures parses identity fields, kernel, obligations, terminals and exclusions; a parametrized corpus of contradictions must fail and smaller equivalent forms must pass.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: reuse the negative/positive corpus pattern but treat it as a bounded oracle (THR-33).

atoms.name: Frozen anchor tripwires
atoms.statement: Tests pin exact digests of protected assets (core tree, adapter, host config), the event-type set, the empty dependency list and the single lock so any change must be explicit.
atoms.mechanism: Anchor test compares sha256/path-tree digests and constant sets; changing a protected file requires updating the literal in the same reviewed change.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: anchor G1's verifier, but keep pins outside the agent-writable tree (see findings).

atoms.name: Independent reproduce-first re-audit
atoms.statement: Every task is re-audited by a non-implementer from a fresh session that treats the report as claims, reproduces each claim in isolated copies with empty HOME, and leaves the original untouched.
atoms.mechanism: Each audit records auditor role, authority order, isolation method and a claim-to-evidence matrix; only the audit file itself is added to the repo.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 audits run in separate sessions with no shared context with the implementer.

atoms.name: Evidence classes with attestation ceiling
atoms.statement: Classify evidence as user-observed, host-observed, repository-bound, runtime-reproducible or not reconstructible, rank code and canonical state above reports, and never claim beyond the class.
atoms.mechanism: Audits emit graded verdicts (PROVEN vs STRONGLY_SUPPORTED vs CONFIGURED_ONLY); deterministic code wins where prose and runtime differ.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 records should carry an evidence-class field.

atoms.name: Report frozen before verification
atoms.statement: The task report is frozen before Public Verify and hashed as an artifact into the success receipt; explicit completion must post-date it and bind that receipt.
atoms.mechanism: Auditors check mtime ordering report < verification_started < verification_succeeded < complete and that the report sha256 equals the receipt artifact hash.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: an agent-written summary is just another hashed artifact, not a claim channel.

atoms.name: Failed attempts preserved as negative evidence
atoms.statement: Failed verification attempts stay immutable in the ledger as negative evidence; remediation proceeds by a new attempt, never by rewriting history.
atoms.mechanism: verification_failed records remain chained; re-audits confirm prior failed attempts are intact and distinct from the successful receipt.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep.

atoms.name: Worker writes harness canonical state
atoms.statement: An agent/delegate with write access can tamper with harness-owned state (oracle, evidence, ledger) undetected when that state is inside its writable area or outside the integrity snapshot, or when isolation is a trusted boolean rather than proof.
atoms.mechanism: Workspaces moved outside root (mkdtemp plus _assert_external), write delegation disabled pending real confinement, tamper made typed; the whole route/delegate subsystem was later deleted.
atoms.threat: Delegate wrote ../../private/oracle.json and still returned status verified (P1); write_isolation=True flag trusted without proof (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: omp's agent can write anything its user can, so G1's evidence store must be outside its reach or hash-anchored externally.

atoms.name: Completion trusted self-reported exit code
atoms.statement: A completion gate that trusts a manifest's self-reported exit_code lets a one-integer edit turn a failed verification into completion.
atoms.mechanism: Completion requires the root-appended verification_succeeded receipt bound to contract and manifest hashes; plan, report, hooks and loops share one evaluator.
atoms.threat: Editing exit_code 1 to 0 passed plan --status complete, report --require-complete and the Stop gate (P1).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 computes success only from the exit status it observed itself.

atoms.name: Evidence fields recorded but never bound
atoms.statement: Evidence fields that are recorded but never recomputed or hash-bound (tree hash, timestamp, stdout/stderr content) accept forged values.
atoms.mechanism: Completion recomputes source digest and git tree, binds receipt and manifest timestamps, and schema-3 manifests carry stdout/stderr SHA-256 repeated in the receipt.
atoms.threat: Fake git_tree_hash 'deadbeef', a 1999 timestamp and edited command.stdout were all accepted (P2/P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: every evidence field must be recomputed by G1 or bound by a hash G1 computed.

atoms.name: Secrets and private oracles leak into evidence
atoms.statement: Verification commands inheriting the full environment and world-readable evidence files leak secrets and private oracle commands/outputs into shareable evidence.
atoms.mechanism: Public evidence records digests/results only, files are 0600 in 0700 dirs, verify runs with a scrubbed sterile HOME/TMP and secret redaction; the oracle path was later deleted.
atoms.threat: Oracle command and stdout appeared in a 0644 manifest; an echoed env secret landed in command.stdout (P2/P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 command capture must scrub env and restrict file modes.

atoms.name: Untyped exceptions escape the gates
atoms.statement: Tamper, lock, decode or permission failures that surface as raw exceptions instead of typed fail-closed codes break uniform handling and can hide every task's result.
atoms.mechanism: Errors normalized to HarnessError codes (ledger_lock_io, ledger_corrupt, EVIDENCE_IO, invalid_manifest) per task, with one core code across all surfaces.
atoms.threat: Uncaught HarnessError/PermissionError/RecursionError/ValueError turned the whole report into internal_error or a traceback (P2-P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 verdicts form a closed typed alphabet; anything else maps to a typed fail-closed error.

atoms.name: Bypass-validated activation claims
atoms.statement: Protection validated only through bypass paths (trust-bypass smoke, disabled production hooks) gets claimed as active protection while the real path never ran.
atoms.mechanism: Doctor separates installed/trusted/active and never reports untrusted hooks active; smoke is labelled transport-only with normal_trust_activation_proven=false; README requires manual trust review.
atoms.threat: Hooks silently inactive until trusted (P1); fixed PreToolUse never ran in production yet 'production failure fixed' was claimed (P2).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 must prove its activation from observed omp events and label test-only paths as such.

atoms.name: Trust hash excludes executed code
atoms.statement: Host trust that hashes only the hook handler definition lets changes to transitively imported harness code alter hook behavior without re-approval.
atoms.mechanism: Not mitigated (host-owned); recorded as a limitation and deferred.
atoms.threat: Codex trust covers the command/wrapper, not src/codex_harness imports, so source edits silently change trusted hook behavior.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: G1 should hash its own loaded code and stamp that digest on every verdict.

atoms.name: Symlink, hardlink and TOCTOU file swaps
atoms.statement: Path checks separated from use, or missing symlink/hardlink/inode checks, let an attacker redirect canonical writes or make the harness hash a different file.
atoms.mechanism: O_NOFOLLOW opens with lstat/fstat inode agreement, dir-fd component walks with fd-based hashing, and single-link regular-file checks for ledger metadata and outputs.
atoms.threat: ledger.jsonl symlink wrote outside the repo; a symlink swap between check and hash; lock inode replacement; manifest hardlink accepted (P3/P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: open agent-controlled files no-follow and hash via the opened descriptor.

atoms.name: History rollback or erasure goes undetected
atoms.statement: A self-validating hash chain without an external anchor or loss detection accepts a truncated prefix or a silently re-created empty ledger, reviving invalidated completions or erasing history.
atoms.mechanism: Ledger v2 head anchor (ledger_id, last seq, record hash, end offset) checked on every surface; pristine vs lost state distinguished by durable traces, genesis only via explicit task begin.
atoms.threat: Deleting the invalidation line revived completion; deleting ledger+head silently re-genesised and erased invalidations (P2).
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the anchor, but place it where the agent cannot write (T1's head is same-user writable).

atoms.name: Superlinear ledger cost blocks availability
atoms.statement: Re-validating the whole hash chain on every append makes append O(n^2) and sessions O(n^3), turning normal growth into a denial of service.
atoms.mechanism: Ledger v2 appends read only the tail via the head anchor (constant parse/hash/fsync work); full verification stays O(n).
atoms.threat: Single append took 687 ms at 500 records and 10k records exceeded 5 minutes (P2; severity first understated as P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: benchmark G1's evidence log at 10k+ records.

atoms.name: Surfaces disagree on the same state
atoms.statement: When different surfaces (stop gate, report, plan, hooks) evaluate different task subsets or logic, one surface passes what another blocks.
atoms.mechanism: A single completion evaluator and one global integrity issue shared by report, doctor, plan and adapters; the Stop hook was ultimately deleted.
atoms.threat: Stop checked only tasks[0] and returned continue:true while report blocked another task's invalidation (P2).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: one verdict function, many projections.

atoms.name: Non-canonical encodings cause parser divergence
atoms.statement: Accepting duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity, bool-as-int, alternate spellings or unbounded sizes lets two parsers read the same bytes differently and lets oversized records strand recovery.
atoms.mechanism: Single bytes-first strict decoder, writer-derived canonical byte equality, exact int types, and exact record/head/pending size limits checked before any write.
atoms.threat: A duplicate-key line read as a forged payload by first-wins parsers; NaN appended; a 3.2 MB payload left a permanently unrecoverable pending journal (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: hash exact canonical bytes and reject anything a second parser could read differently.

atoms.name: Lock liveness and identity hazards
atoms.statement: Blocking locks without timeout, lock files replaceable by inode swap, and lock-free status reads cause indefinite hangs, lost mutual exclusion or false alarms.
atoms.mechanism: Partially mitigated: one canonical flock with open-time no-follow/inode checks and shared-lock reads; the flock still blocks without timeout and there is no post-acquire inode recheck.
atoms.threat: A SIGSTOPped holder hangs every surface; rm+touch of ledger.lock let two writers append seq 2 (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: modify: use bounded lock waits and verify lock identity after acquisition.

atoms.name: Environment override redirects canonical writes
atoms.statement: Root discovery that prefers an environment variable over the event's working directory or explicit root lets a write land in a different repository.
atoms.mechanism: Hook root derived from the wrapper's own file path (symlink boundary refused) plus an event-cwd Git-root check; HARNESS_ROOT redirection removed and smoke runs with a scrubbed env.
atoms.threat: HARNESS_ROOT=A with cwd B appended hook events into A; smoke children inherited HARNESS_ROOT (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: derive the workspace root from observed facts, never from agent-settable env.

atoms.name: Residue and leaked resources pollute state
atoms.statement: Leftover worktrees, temp files, caches, bytecode and stray copies accumulate and leak into digests or repo-wide scans, changing what gets verified.
atoms.mechanism: Cleanup in finally on all outcomes, -B/PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, --no-cache lint, digest exclusions, residue-absence tests and per-test fixture teardown.
atoms.threat: Orphan worktrees; .tmp files after crashes; .pyc from hooks; .ruff_cache from Public Verify; an in-repo sdcard/ draft copy entered source_digest; fixture trees broke the single-spec scan (P2-P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: snapshot the workspace before/after G1 actions and fail on unexplained residue.

atoms.name: Tool-gating hook blocks its own lifecycle
atoms.statement: A pre-tool gating hook with a shell classifier denies legitimate verification and lifecycle commands, blocks subagents and reimplements native approvals.
atoms.mechanism: PreToolUse, the 474-LOC side-effect classifier and approval regexes were deleted; the generated manifest has SessionStart only and no ordinary-tool hook.
atoms.threat: With an active task, pytest, ruff, verify and complete were denied (19/31); Agent/spawn_agent always denied (P1/P2).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 observes tool calls instead of vetoing them; vetoes self-DoS the harness.

atoms.name: Non-authoritative events enter canonical history
atoms.statement: Telemetry, denial, advisory-hook or retired events written to (or replayed into) the canonical ledger get misread as invalidations and pollute authority.
atoms.mechanism: Writer allowlist of 7 current event types enforced on append and on pending replay; hooks are zero-write; retired events stay readable but inert.
atoms.threat: A denied, never-run command logged as pretool_blocked invalidated a valid verification (P1); ledger recover committed a retired codex_takeover (P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: separate G1's tool-call observation log from its verdict ledger; only verdict events change authority.

atoms.name: Historical validity tied to current source
atoms.statement: Requiring every past completion to match the current source makes any unrelated edit invalidate all history and forces endless re-verification.
atoms.mechanism: Historical completion is evaluated against its recorded receipt (immutable snapshot); only the current task is checked against current source (require_current).
atoms.threat: Adding one unrelated file flipped four completed tasks to SOURCE_CHANGED; 9 of 16 verifications were re-verifications.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: distinguish 'verified at receipt' from 'valid now'.

atoms.name: Turn-end gate forces unwanted continuation
atoms.statement: A stop/turn-end hook that blocks while criteria are incomplete forces extra model continuations, nags parked tasks and breaks intentional pause or context-clear boundaries.
atoms.mechanism: Stop was shown to own no unique invariant and was physically deleted; projection is SessionStart-only and parked tasks are not projected.
atoms.threat: A trusted Stop hook forced a continuation at a clear gate (STOP_HOOK_ROTATION_CONFLICT) and failed the E2E; Stop appended unbounded records (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 never forces an omp turn to continue; it only refuses completion claims.

atoms.name: Empty versus corrupt state confusion
atoms.statement: Treating an empty plan as invalid breaks fresh bootstrap, while treating a corrupt or zero-byte plan as 'no tasks' yields vacuous success.
atoms.mechanism: Zero-task template is valid and task begin creates the first contract; zero-byte/header-less plans are invalid; plan/ledger mismatch is reported; Goal completion is never derived from an empty report.
atoms.threat: A placeholder task blocked every Stop in fresh repos (P2); a truncated plan read as 'no T1 tasks' passed Stop and report (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: 'nothing to check' must never be reported as 'checked and passed'.

atoms.name: Unbound or legacy completion paths
atoms.statement: Completion transitions without explicit receipt binding (latest-success fallback, raw API append, migration import) let unrelated or later receipts satisfy completion or silently downgrade strict tasks.
atoms.mechanism: New transitions must bind receipt seq and hash (completion_binding_required); legacy fallback is prefix-bounded; v1 migration was deleted and v1 input is typed unsupported.
atoms.threat: A later bogus success changed history; Ledger.append wrote an unbound complete; ledger migrate manufactured a legacy completion (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: every completion names the exact receipt it rests on.

atoms.name: Later attempts overwrite earlier evidence
atoms.statement: Single-path evidence lets a new verify attempt overwrite earlier outputs, destroying a completed task's historical proof or a failed attempt's diagnostics.
atoms.mechanism: verify refuses completed tasks (verification_refused_complete_task) at both plan-status and ledger-authority boundaries before any write; failed-attempt outputs are still overwritten (only digests survive).
atoms.threat: Re-verifying a completed task made report --require-complete fail repo-wide with MANIFEST_CHANGED (P2); failed-attempt stdout lost (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: modify: make G1 evidence per-attempt and append-only so nothing is overwritten.

atoms.name: Check-then-act races outside the lock
atoms.statement: Guards evaluated before acquiring the mutation lock can be passed by two racing processes, letting a loser overwrite evidence or duplicate records.
atoms.mechanism: Frontier checks run under the single exclusive ledger lock (completion_binding_stale; verification_started refused after completion; invalidation read and append in one critical section).
atoms.threat: A verify started inside complete's evaluate-to-append window overwrote the manifest (2/6 runs, P2); concurrent invalidations appended twice (P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: every G1 decision re-reads state under the same lock it writes under.

atoms.name: Terminal state bypassed by edits
atoms.statement: Completed tasks can be silently reopened or rewritten when status changes or contract amendments are not terminal-checked on every mutation path.
atoms.mechanism: complete-to-any transitions and amendments refused (task_reopen_refused); terminality holds if either plan status or the ledger transition says complete, including raw API appends.
atoms.threat: plan --status active then verify replaced evidence and re-bound completion; --accept-contract-change on a completed task destroyed history (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: closed tasks are immutable; new work needs a new task.

atoms.name: False conflated with cannot tell
atoms.statement: Reporting false for a check that could not run (missing hash, unreadable file) makes 'undetectable' indistinguishable from 'verified unchanged'.
atoms.mechanism: historical_manifest_rewritten became tri-state true/false/null with manifest_binding_available exposed; hash or I/O failures yield null plus a typed code.
atoms.threat: mvp's receipt lacked manifest_content_hash, so a rewritten manifest showed rewritten=false (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: every G1 check result is pass/fail/unknown, never boolean.

atoms.name: Dual-write crash window strands state
atoms.statement: A crash between two non-atomic writes (ledger append then plan replace) can leave a state that newly added guards refuse forever.
atoms.mechanism: Idempotent self-recovery: a retry that finds an identical committed transition (same contract and receipt) only replaces the plan; non-complete statuses reconcile exactly once.
atoms.threat: A kill after the complete append left ledger complete/plan active, refused by completion_binding_stale with no exit but contract amendment (P2 regression).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: inject kills between every pair of writes and require convergence.

atoms.name: Lost updates reported as success
atoms.statement: Read-modify-replace file updates without a lock or compare-and-swap silently drop concurrent writers' changes while every caller reports success.
atoms.mechanism: The single ledger.lock now spans plan replace plus ledger append for all cooperative writers; losers get typed zero-write conflicts.
atoms.threat: Two concurrent activations both returned rc 0; the plan kept one while the ledger recorded both (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: one lock covers every co-dependent write.

atoms.name: Read-only surfaces that actually write
atoms.statement: Status, report, hook or audit commands assumed read-only can still write (git objects, index.lock, bytecode, caches, smoke evidence), mutating what later checks see.
atoms.mechanism: doctor/report never compute source/tree digests; hooks run with -B under zero-write snapshot tests; audits recommend GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0; remaining writes are documented.
atoms.threat: An active Stop wrote loose git objects; resume --dry-run created objects; hooks wrote .pyc; a read-only git status created index.lock (P3/P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: verify read-only claims with before/after filesystem snapshots, including .git.

atoms.name: Verifier weakened during reduction
atoms.statement: Deleting or loosening tests/checks while simplifying removes security coverage, and reports may still claim that coverage passes.
atoms.mechanism: Re-audits diff test inventories against prior trees and restored the deleted boundary tests; O12 forbids weaker verifiers as gain; test-only fixes are checked for assertion weakening.
atoms.threat: Five security-boundary tests vanished while the report said they 'continue to pass' (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: pin G1's test inventory and fail when a check disappears.

atoms.name: Tests depend on live mutable state
atoms.statement: Tests that read live harness state (e.g., counting completed tasks) go red once the task under test completes, making every later Public Verify fail.
atoms.mechanism: The test now asserts a frozen ID subset with exact receipts instead of a live count; the residual live-state read is documented.
atoms.threat: The suite was 280/281 after the task's own completion; the implementer's '281 passed' held only pre-completion (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 acceptance tests must be hermetic or pinned to frozen IDs.

atoms.name: Caller overrides contract-declared evidence
atoms.statement: Letting the verifier's caller substitute evidence targets (e.g., --artifact) lets completion succeed on artifacts the contract never declared.
atoms.mechanism: The override was deleted; verify always hashes exactly the contract's Artifacts in order and records missing ones as typed verification failures.
atoms.threat: verify --artifact other.txt then complete succeeded for a task declaring artifact.txt (P3, pre-existing).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: the agent never chooses which evidence G1 checks.

atoms.name: Unbounded scope accepted as bounded
atoms.statement: Path validators that normalize '.' to an empty path accept the entire repository as a 'bounded' task scope.
atoms.mechanism: Allowed paths with empty parts (root-equivalent) are rejected directly before a registration is accepted.
atoms.threat: A selected task with Allowed path '.' claimed the whole repo and could declare protected files as artifacts (P2).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: canonicalize, then reject root-equivalent or escaping scopes.

atoms.name: Text-pattern oracles defeated by paraphrase
atoms.statement: Keyword/regex checkers over prose (giant-task detection, spec contradiction corpus) are bounded oracles that paraphrased or gutted-but-consistent text passes.
atoms.mechanism: Declared as bounded and left unremediated; real behavior is constrained by runtime gates (Public Verify, receipt binding, audits).
atoms.threat: 'Deliver the whole local release candidate end to end' passed the giant-task filter (P3); gutted obligation bodies pass the spec checker (P2-info).
atoms.g1_hint: drop: never rely on text matching of model output for safety; gate on executed evidence.

atoms.name: Claiming another process's operation
atoms.statement: Attributing any observed new state change to 'my' invocation lets a run claim a registration caused by a peer or external writer.
atoms.mechanism: Each launch generates a 128-bit nonce carried once in the prompt; selected only if the sole new task echoes it exactly, otherwise protocol_error with a null claim.
atoms.threat: Two concurrent selectors both reported selected/task-beta though one child failed (P3); the nonce is correlation, not authentication (argv-visible).
atoms.g1_hint: modify: attribute effects via G1's own recorded tool-call IDs, not a model-echoed nonce.

atoms.name: Goal completion by self-declared coverage
atoms.statement: A final task whose contract merely declares it checked every terminal property can yield goal_complete if its Public Verify is weak.
atoms.mechanism: goal_complete re-derives receipt currency and source/tree binding, but aggregate coverage is delegated to the final task's Public Verify and the P09/P10 audit gate (open).
atoms.threat: A weak-but-textually-final completed task would report goal_complete (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: modify: G1 maps each terminal property to a check it runs itself.

atoms.name: Digest blind to mode and file type
atoms.statement: A source digest that omits executable bits or type tags misses meaningful changes (chmod +x, file/symlink swaps, symlink-to-dir) and misclassifies them as no progress.
atoms.mechanism: source_digest entries bind type, content hash, size and executable bit (regular) or raw target hash (symlink) via lstat; FIFO/socket fail closed as unsupported_source_type.
atoms.threat: chmod 0644 to 0755 and same-content file/symlink swaps were classified no_durable_progress (P2/P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1's workspace fingerprint includes type and exec bit and fails on special files.

atoms.name: Out-of-band tampering reported as clean
atoms.statement: Direct edits to completed or parked task records (criteria, objective, status resurrection) leave report/doctor clean when integrity checks skip non-current tasks or short-circuit on the active branch.
atoms.mechanism: One global historical_task_integrity_regression compares every task's contract anchor, recorded completion and latest status anchor, including the active task; adapters fail closed before launch.
atoms.threat: Flipping a completed criterion [x] to [ ] and editing Status: complete to active stayed silent (P2/P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: cross-check every task record against its ledger anchors each turn.

atoms.name: No-op turn counted as progress
atoms.statement: A turn that exits 0 without any durable change, if reported as ordinary 'active', lets a loop spin forever.
atoms.mechanism: A before/after durable snapshot (source digest, criteria, status, verification frontier) yields typed no_durable_progress; the supervisor stops after 2 consecutive no-progress turns.
atoms.threat: A no-op fake codex was reported active (exit 10) indefinitely.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: progress is a harness-measured durable delta, never the agent saying it progressed.

atoms.name: Loops that never converge
atoms.statement: Execution loops oscillate between equivalent states (A to B to A, verify-only history churn) or run unbounded unless state is fingerprinted and turns/episodes are hard-capped.
atoms.mechanism: Semantic fingerprint (task, contract, status, criteria, verification state, source digest; excluding seq/timestamps) with a seen-set, MAX_ACTIVE_TURNS=8 and a 32-episode budget, terminal outcomes taking precedence.
atoms.threat: A-B-A cycles and verify-only appends that never finish the task.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: fingerprint semantic state, not history, and hard-cap turns.

atoms.name: Child process hangs without deadline
atoms.statement: Without a wall-clock deadline per child invocation, one hung or partially-writing child blocks the controller forever; turn counts bound count, not duration.
atoms.mechanism: Finite child deadline plus grace, then process-group termination and typed child_timeout; partial JSON never bypasses the deadline.
atoms.threat: Sleeping selector/active children and a grandchild holding stdout hung the supervisor (P2).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: every process G1 launches gets a hard deadline.

atoms.name: Unbounded child output capture
atoms.statement: Capturing a child's whole stdout before size validation lets a flooding child exhaust controller memory.
atoms.mechanism: Incremental bounded reads capped at the protocol limit (1024 bytes plus one), terminating the child on overflow with a typed protocol_error.
atoms.threat: An infinite producer drove supervisor RSS to 3.2 GiB in 6 s (P2).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: cap every captured stream G1 reads.

atoms.name: Descendants escape and keep mutating
atoms.statement: Children and grandchildren outside a managed process group, or orphaned by a hard-killed parent, keep running and mutating state, and a restarted controller can overlap them.
atoms.mechanism: Children run in a new process group killed TERM then KILL; the driver is a subreaper with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG and reconciles adopted descendants before the next episode; a supervisor script flock prevents overlapping episodes.
atoms.threat: Supervisor SIGKILL left its adapter alive and a replacement started a second adapter (P2); setsid/double-fork descendants survive (P3/P4 residual).
atoms.g1_hint: modify: prefer cgroups/PID namespaces where available; POSIX groups cannot catch setsid escapes.

atoms.name: Stale terminal outcome accepted
atoms.statement: Accepting a child's terminal outcome (complete/blocked) without post-cleanup revalidation lets descendant writes after the decision make it stale.
atoms.mechanism: Supervisor outcomes are only hints: the driver cleans up, requires two stable post-cleanup observations and re-runs the task/goal O8 gate with require_current before advancing.
atoms.threat: A grandchild's write landed after the direct child emitted complete, and the supervisor emitted task_complete anyway (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: re-verify after all child processes are reaped, never at the moment of the claim.

atoms.name: Single-flight keyed to wrong identity
atoms.statement: A mutual-exclusion lock keyed to a script inode instead of the protected resource lets copies bypass it and serializes unrelated repositories.
atoms.mechanism: The driver adds a repository-scoped non-blocking directory guard; the supervisor's inode lock remains a disclosed P4.
atoms.threat: A byte-identical copy at another inode ran concurrently in the same repo (P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: key locks to the workspace identity.

atoms.name: Protocol validator fidelity errors
atoms.statement: Inter-process protocol validators can be too strict (rejecting reachable legitimate outcomes) or too loose (accepting unpinned informational fields).
atoms.mechanism: The validator accepts exactly the producer's reachable last-child outcomes and is tested against the real producer; informational-field permissiveness is documented P4.
atoms.threat: turn_budget_exhausted after a final no_durable_progress turn was misreported as protocol_error (P2); resealed evidence with altered informational fields verified (P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: derive the accepted alphabet from the producer's reachable states and test against the real producer.

atoms.name: Done versus next-task ambiguity
atoms.statement: A stateless turn boundary cannot distinguish 'goal achieved' from 'next task not yet registered', so a loop stops after one task or needs a giant task or hidden memory.
atoms.mechanism: Master Goal spec plus no-active selector plus multi-task driver: no_active triggers one selection turn and goal_complete is derived only from the final receipt.
atoms.threat: The supervisor stopped after task A with no path to a second task.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: G1 needs an explicit terminal spec so 'no work' is never mistaken for 'done'.

atoms.name: Spec bloat with dead constructs
atoms.statement: Normative specs accumulate dead symbols, removable formulas and duplicated statements that cost interpretation without adding rejection power.
atoms.mechanism: Mutation/deletion attacks on the spec found removable blocks; the compressed spec is zero-symbol, formula-free and checker-pinned against re-growth.
atoms.threat: Four dead symbols, two removable formula blocks and prose/formula duplication (P2); 9 axioms reducible to 5 (P3).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: keep G1's rule spec minimal and mutation-tested.

atoms.name: Checker overfit to current prose
atoms.statement: A checker of hard-coded strings rejects meaning-preserving smaller rewrites, blocking legitimate simplification.
atoms.mechanism: Data-driven checker with semantic regexes plus an equivalence corpus that must still pass (shorter authority, merged kernels, glyph variants).
atoms.threat: About 115 hard-coded strings rejected glyph variants and paraphrases of required sentences (P2).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: pair every negative corpus with a positive equivalence corpus.

atoms.name: Host-specific instruction leaks into repo
atoms.statement: Host-specific standing instructions (a fixed /sdcard draft copy) in always-read instructions get applied wrongly and leak residue into the verified tree.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md bullet replaced with a host-neutral optional-copy rule and residue cleaned; the Goal checker forbids host paths, but AGENTS.md itself is only size-checked.
atoms.threat: A relative-path copy created sdcard/abc/t1/draft/... inside the repo, which entered source_digest and the verified tree (P3/P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: lint G1's injected instructions for host paths, not just the spec.

atoms.name: Scope creep into unneeded subsystems
atoms.statement: Agents add subsystems without proven need (tool classifier, routing/delegation, resume loops, migration, private oracle, context rollover), expanding attack surface and leaking authority.
atoms.mechanism: Audits issue DELETE/NOT_NEEDED verdicts backed by usage counts; deletion tasks removed them with negative tests asserting absence.
atoms.threat: Route/delegate was always imported and the sole writer of invalidation events; rollover was proposed without an observed need.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: require a reproduced need before G1 grows a component.

atoms.name: Derived artifacts mistaken for authority
atoms.statement: Caches, backups and reports that look canonical can be consumed as authority or go stale silently.
atoms.mechanism: cache/report.json was deleted (no reader); report is derived on demand and writes nothing; the v1 backup is never restored as canonical.
atoms.threat: A write-only cache with zero readers and a backup that could be mistaken for truth.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 recomputes views; it never trusts a cached verdict.

atoms.name: Fake or redirected provider passes as real
atoms.statement: Environment overrides (base URL, fake-boundary flags, PATH shadowing) can swap the real agent/provider for a mock while evidence still looks like a real run.
atoms.mechanism: Native E2E rejects fake/redirect env names, builds an allowlisted env, pins config without provider overrides, verifies executable path and sha256 per process, and grades transport STRONGLY_SUPPORTED, not PROVEN.
atoms.threat: Mock transport or a shadowed codex binary producing E2E evidence.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: record binary hash and effective env for every agent process G1 observes.

atoms.name: Frozen evidence tampered and resealed
atoms.statement: Self-describing evidence documents can be edited and resealed unless a canonical self-hash, an external receipt and a broad tamper matrix pin every gated field.
atoms.mechanism: Canonical self-hash, root-receipt sealing of the artifact hash, strict JSON (duplicates/NaN rejected), secret-shape rejection and a 69-mutation tamper matrix.
atoms.threat: Resealed variants changing informational fields or adding a fake process record still verified (P4).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: seal G1 evidence with an external anchor; a self-hash alone is resealable.

atoms.name: Hidden context smuggled as continuity
atoms.statement: Continuity that silently relies on hidden conversation, memory or session state passes ordinary tests yet violates reconstruction-only continuity.
atoms.mechanism: The E2E plants a durable marker (must be recovered) and an ephemeral nonce (must be unrecoverable from authority) across real /clear boundaries; continuity env IDs are excluded.
atoms.threat: An agent recovering a value only present in prior conversation context.
atoms.g1_hint: experiment: adopt the marker/nonce test to prove G1 continuity is reconstruction-only.

atoms.name: Model prose drives control decisions
atoms.statement: Controllers that parse model text or unstable output to decide outcomes can be steered by the model.
atoms.mechanism: Adapters emit one bounded typed JSON line and exit code; stderr is forwarded but never parsed; supervisor/driver contain no model invocation and reject cross-role outcomes.
atoms.threat: A model printing 'goal complete' or crafted text to steer the loop.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: G1 branches only on harness-observed facts, never on LLM text.

atoms.name: Implementer reports overclaim or understate
atoms.statement: Implementation reports overstate results (fixed in production, no new P1, tests pass, check counts) or understate severity and omit residual attack paths.
atoms.mechanism: Each claim gets a claim-to-evidence matrix row reproduced by an independent auditor; discrepancies are logged as findings.
atoms.threat: 'Production failure fixed' and 'no new P0/P1' were false; F11 severity understated; tail truncation omitted from residuals; smoke checks miscounted.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: treat every agent report as a list of claims to re-execute.

atoms.name: Premature completion claims
atoms.statement: Agents claim completion before verification exists or present historical completion as current verification.
atoms.mechanism: Reports are frozen before Public Verify and bound as artifacts; completion requires a later receipt-bound transition; auditors check report < started < succeeded < complete ordering.
atoms.threat: A report asserts done while no verification_succeeded receipt exists.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: a 'done' message without a G1-observed receipt is logged as a false claim.

atoms.name: Remediations introduce regressions
atoms.statement: A fix for one finding can create new failure modes (stuck states, weakened legacy checks) unless the whole boundary is re-audited, including crash windows.
atoms.mechanism: Every remediation gets a full independent re-audit with crash and concurrency matrices before readiness advances.
atoms.threat: The G1 race fix created the H1 permanent stuck state; core isolation dropped manifest checks a prior audit relied on.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: re-run the full adversarial matrix after every fix.

atoms.name: Self-approval and non-independent audit
atoms.statement: An implementer approving its own work, or an audit drawing on auxiliary models/subagents, cannot count as verification.
atoms.mechanism: Auditors are non-implementers in fresh sessions with recorded process compliance (substantive auditor, zero subagents/auxiliary models); O12 rejects self-approval.
atoms.threat: An implementer signing off its own claims.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: the agent under test never grades itself.

findings.detail: Same-OS-user threat boundary: T1 assumes a single cooperative root writer; a same-user process can coherently rewrite plan, ledger, head and evidence (the head anchor sits beside the ledger and is same-user writable), which T1 scopes out but a paranoid G1 must not.
N9 never remediated: the canonical flock blocks with no timeout, so a stopped holder hangs every surface (N8-N13 were explicitly not claimed fixed).
N10 never remediated: lock identity is checked only at open time; there is no post-acquire inode recheck, so a replaced lock file can break mutual exclusion.
Detached (setsid/double-fork) descendants and simultaneous external hard kills escape POSIX process-group cleanup; a cgroup/service boundary is required before 24x7 use.
Host hook trust hashes only the handler/wrapper definition, not transitively imported harness code; deferred as host-owned.
Prose checkers are bounded oracles with no remediation planned: gutted-but-consistent obligations, wrong-property evidence containing a deterministic token, and paraphrased giant tasks pass.
Goal-terminal coverage is declaration-checked: goal_complete trusts the final task's own Public Verify for all ten properties.
Selection operation nonce is correlation, not authentication (forced collision or same-user argv forgery is attributable), and it is stored as an acceptance criterion for lack of a metadata channel.
Real provider transport and remote model identity are not attested (STRONGLY_SUPPORTED / CONFIGURED_ONLY); evidence is anchored in config, binary hashes and root receipts only.
Explicit invalidation is accepted on completed (terminal) tasks; whether that override is intended was never decided and remains deferred.
git_tree_hash snapshots write loose objects into .git/objects on every verification/completion with no bound or gc policy.
Informational fields of the supervisor payload and frozen E2E evidence are not pinned (resealed variants accepted); documented as P4, not fixed.
Canonical file modes (plan 0644/0666, ledger/head 0644) are not enforced on the read path; only write paths restore 0600.
O(1) ordinary append validates only the tail record, so middle-of-ledger corruption is caught only by full verify or full-read events.
report --require-complete is vacuously true for a zero-task plan; Goal authority is separate, but any consumer gating on report.complete gets a vacuous pass.
Native in-turn compaction is possible and unbounded inside a single agent turn; only small atomic tasks mitigate it.
Evidence uses one fixed path per task (manifest.json, command.stdout, command.stderr), so a failed attempt's raw output is overwritten by the next attempt; only ledger digests survive (M10).

AGENTS.md and skill rules (no completion claim without evidence, read policy, host neutrality) are advisory text; the checker validates only AGENTS.md size, and model chat claims are unconstrained except by the CLI completion gate.
Frozen-anchor tripwires (exact digests in tests) live in the same agent-writable tree as the code they pin, so a single change can update both; they detect accidents, not a coordinated agent.
Canonical runtime state is git-ignored, so a git-only clone is lost state; cross-host moves must carry .harness, and a historical test still reads the live .harness.
docs/AUDIT.md is a stale baseline (Codex CLI 0.150.1, pre-reduction surfaces) while later audits run 0.151.0 with a SessionStart-only manifest.
Atom loc values are approximate: audit-stated deltas where available, whole-module size where the mechanism is a module, and 0 for principles or deleted mechanisms.
